graph.title: Billund Airport
notes: Element IDs were read from the inventory page; several steps show only pictures, so a few part identities (e.g. 1x3 white plates vs. 302201, 1x1 stacks in steps 23/26) are best guesses. Some inventory IDs not in the catalogue were added as new types.
The base is four 6x12 black plates (302826) joined side by side via overlapping 1x6/1x1 border tiles; the exact seam-by-seam tile coverage is simplified.

Ground-level pieces (steps 9-16) are attached to the nearest base plate (b7, b10 or b13) rather than to each other, since exact stud positions are not given in the pictures. Pieces in those steps that sit on other ground pieces are likewise simplified.

Step 17 (jet bridge plate + tile on the stud tile) and step 50 (five aeroplanes) are merged into one repeat 'gate' x5; aeroplane colours (red/blue, white/red, white/dark-blue, blue/yellow, white/light-blue) are given as overrides. The plane wing tile only rests on the tail slope and cockpit slope (contact edges). The base-plate type for the plane (302201) is an assumption.
Step 19 (4 terminal roof units) is a repeat 'term'; the internal stacking order is partly inferred. The steps 20-42 assemblies are placed on nearby plates with approximate attachment points.

Steps 45-47 flowers: 4 orange+white stacks and 4 blue+lime stacks (3 additional lime round plates in step 45 are placed separately). Flagpole bar is plugged into a green plate stud (b65); the red flag plate clips onto its top.
Tile pieces have no studs, so nothing attaches onto them; the 1x1 tiles in step 17/19 etc. are placed on plates only.
